notes: THE FIXED-ASSET REGISTER NOW STOPS WHEN IT CANNOT READ THE DEPRECIATION HISTORY. Running depreciation, disposing, revaluing, and changing a cost or opening figure are all refused until the history can be read — with the reason shown. Previously every asset read as never depreciated, so a year-end run could charge months already charged and a disposal could write back depreciation the ledger does not hold. The refusal lives in the posting itself, so a form already open when the fault appears cannot slip past it. ARCHIVED DOCUMENTS ARE REACHABLE AGAIN past 500 attachments — the "Show archived" control was being hidden by a count taken from the shortened list rather than from the vault. LONG LISTS STATE THE REAL TOTAL they are not showing (audit log, cheques, lodgements, exchange rates, invoices, petty cash, staff advances, vendor bills) and name the report that reads everything. The cheque register's note was rewritten: that list already carries every outstanding cheque however old, so reconciliation was never affected. UNDOING A REVALUATION NOW RESTORES THE OPENING DEPRECIATION it cleared — for an asset brought in from a previous system that is most of its accumulated depreciation, and it was lost for good. A COMMITMENT NOW RECORDS ITS REQUISITION, so an interrupted conversion cannot hold budget twice. AND FOUR EMPTY SCREENS that said "nothing has been recorded yet" now say whether it was a filter, an archived view, or a failed read. DATABASE CHANGE: two column-only additions. Your books are untouched and this installs over the previous version. Take a backup first all the same — Backup & Export, Back up now.
